weeks.title: What Kind of Peace Are We Waiting For?

blocks.text: What kind of peace are we waiting for?
This week we explore the peace announced at the birth of Jesus.
We ask what that peace means for those who follow the Prince of Peace.
Glory to God in the highest heaven, and on earth peace…
Take your time. Read it slowly, then tap Next.
When you hear the word “peace,” what comes to mind?

blocks.prompt: Write a few words, or just think about it.

blocks.text: Therefore, since we are justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ.

blocks.title: Key Thought
blocks.text: Christian peace begins not with our efforts, but with the grace of God. Through Jesus Christ, God reconciles, redeems, and restores. Walking in the way of peace is our response to grace, not our attempt to earn it.
Tap a question to think about it and write your answer.

items.q: What does it mean to have peace with God?
How is peace with God different from simply feeling peaceful?
Why must our understanding of peace begin with God’s grace?

steps.title: The Peace of Christ Is Different
steps.label: Part 2

blocks.text: Peace I leave with you; my peace I give to you. I do not give to you as the world gives.
Each card looks like peace. Tap it to see what is missing.
Can I claim to possess the peace of Christ while consistently creating turmoil for everybody around me?
Jesus Christ is the Prince of Peace. God gives us peace through Christ. Our peaceful living becomes a response to God’s grace.
Instead of beginning with “Why isn’t the world more peaceful?” what happens when we first ask:
Lord, where do You need to make me more peaceful?
Where is God calling me to practice peace? Tap each circle.

items.name: Peace With God
items.q: What do I need to entrust more fully to God?

items.name: Peace Within Myself
items.q: What fear, guilt, resentment, anxiety, or burden do I need to bring honestly before God?

items.name: Peace With Others
items.q: Where might God be calling me to listen, forgive, apologize, speak truthfully, or stop contributing to unnecessary conflict?

items.name: Peace in the World
items.q: Where do I see division, injustice, suffering, or hostility that calls for faithful Christian concern?

blocks.text: You do not have to share what you write. This is between you and God unless you choose otherwise.
Choose one intentional act of peace this week.

options: Let go of an unnecessary argument
Pray for someone with whom I disagree
Speak a needed word with kindness

steps.title: At the End of the Week

blocks.text: What did practicing peace require of me?

blocks.prompt: Come back later this week and write here.

blocks.title: Remember
blocks.text: The question is not, Did the other person change? The question is, Was I faithful to Christ?
Glory to God in the highest heaven, and on earth peace…
May God grant us the grace to practice the peace for which we pray.
Amen.
